name: Avoid process control through API requests
associatedValueName: Call stack from external input source down to the target method
description:
Using CAST data-flow engine, this quality rule identifies code paths where API request parameters flow directly to system call API methods that can load libraries. The rule tracks data flow from API-based input sources (such as REST endpoints, web service parameters, or API calls) down to sensitive library loading functions.
This quality rule focuses specifically on preventing unauthorized library loading by detecting when API request data can influence which libraries or assemblies are loaded into the application's process space. Unlike direct user input scenarios, this rule targets vulnerabilities where external systems or API consumers can manipulate library loading through API parameters.
output:
List all methods that make log method calls forged by user-controllable data from API requests

It provides the following information:
 - Method full name
 - Call stack from API request down to the target method.
rationale:
When API request parameters directly influence library loading operations, attackers can inject malicious library names or paths to:
-Load malicious libraries that compromise application security
-Execute arbitrary code through malicious dynamic libraries (DLLs, shared objects)
-Bypass security controls by loading unauthorized modules
-Gain elevated privileges through library injection attacks
-Access sensitive system resources through crafted library paths
This vulnerability is particularly dangerous because loaded libraries execute with the same privileges as the host application. Attackers can exploit path traversal vulnerabilities (e.g., "../../../malicious.dll") or inject completely different library names to load malicious code. The impact ranges from information disclosure to complete system compromise, as malicious libraries can hook into application functions and intercept sensitive operations.

remediation:
Avoid using API request parameters to control library loading. If it is not possible:
-Input validation: implement strict whitelist validation allowing only known-good library identifiers
-Path restriction: use only predefined library paths and validate against directory traversal
-Library mapping: map user input to predefined library names through configuration
-Path canonicalization: resolve and validate library paths before loading
alternativeName: Ensure you don't use external library given by unsanitized user input
